This is good as is — the logic is small and clear. Final summary of the change:

**`habit done` now accepts an optional trailing date** — `habit done read`, `habit done read yesterday`, or `habit done read 2026-09-01`.

- `src/streak.js`: added `parseDay(token, now)`, returning a `Date` for `"today"`/`"yesterday"`/`YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` if the token isn't a recognized date.
- `src/cli.js`: when `done` gets more than one arg, it tries to parse the last one as a date; if it parses, that's the date and the rest is the habit name (so multi-word names like `morning run` still work), otherwise the whole thing is just the name and it defaults to today.
- `commands.js`'s `done(name, today)` was untouched — it already accepted a `Date`.
- Added tests: `parseDay` unit tests in `test/streak.test.js`, plus a new `test/cli.test.js` that spawns the real CLI to verify `yesterday`, an ISO date, no date, and multi-word names end-to-end.
- Updated `README.md` with the new usage examples.

All 14 tests pass (`npm test`). Note: I couldn't run ad-hoc shell smoke tests directly in this session (no approval surface for Bash), so I verified behavior via the new `test/cli.test.js` integration tests instead, which spawn the actual CLI binary.
